faqs.question: Is it better to become resident before opening a bank account?
answer: In many cases, yes. UAE residency usually makes the banking process more straightforward and gives banks greater comfort. It also opens access to a wider range of banking options.

faqs.question: Can non-residents open bank accounts in the UAE?
answer: Yes, but the process is usually more restrictive and document-heavy. Non-resident applications often face deeper KYC review and narrower account options.

faqs.question: What should come first-company, visa, or bank account?
answer: For most entrepreneurs, the usual sequence is company first, then residency, then bank account opening. This gives the bank a clearer commercial story and stronger supporting documents.

faqs.question: Why do bank applications get delayed?
answer: The most common reasons are weak documentation, unclear business activity, inconsistent profile information, or insufficient evidence of source of funds and business substance.

faqs.question: Do I need a company to get a Golden Visa?
answer: No.
You can qualify through:
• Property investment (AED 2M+)
• Salary (AED 30,000+)
• Bank deposit (AED 2M+)
Business setup is not required in these cases.

faqs.question: What are the main Golden Visa routes (2026)?
answer: • Property Investor (AED 2M+)
• High Salary Professional (AED 30K/month)
• Fixed Deposit (AED 2M)
• Entrepreneur / Startup Founder
• Specialized Professionals (Doctors, Engineers, IT)
• Outstanding Talent (Arts, Sports, Digital)
• Students / Researchers

faqs.question: Is the Golden Visa linked to corporate tax?
answer: No.
Corporate tax depends on business activity, not your residency type.

faqs.question: Can I stay outside UAE for long periods?
answer: Yes.
Golden Visa holders are not restricted by the 6-month rule.

faqs.question: Is Golden Visa enough for banking?
answer: While the Golden Visa strengthens your profile, banking decisions are still based on overall financial credibility, documentation quality, and commercial rationale.

faqs.question: Should I buy property mainly for residency?
answer: Residency can be a benefit, but property should not be bought only for visa purposes. The asset itself still needs to make sense in terms of quality, pricing, holding period, and overall financial fit.

faqs.question: Can property and business planning be linked?
answer: Yes. For many clients, property, residency, and business presence are connected. Planning them together usually leads to better decisions than treating them as separate moves.

faqs.question: Is real estate always the right first investment in the UAE?
answer: No. It depends on your liquidity, objectives, and timeline. In some cases property makes sense early. In others, it should come after business and residency are properly structured.

faqs.question: Should investment be held personally or through a structure?
answer: That depends on the nature of the investment, family planning considerations, and long-term structuring objectives. This is exactly why the decision should be reviewed before purchase, not after.

faqs.question: When should I start succession planning?
answer: Earlier than most people think. Succession planning should begin once meaningful assets, business interests, or family responsibilities start building. Waiting too long usually reduces flexibility.

faqs.question: Where does life insurance fit into long-term planning?
answer: Life insurance can support family protection, liquidity planning, and continuity. It should be considered as part of the wider structure, not as a standalone purchase.

faqs.question: Is retirement planning relevant if I am still actively building my business?
answer: Yes. Retirement planning is not only about stopping work. It is about long-term financial direction, future residence choices, and how current decisions support later stability.

faqs.question: Why include child education planning here?
answer: Because education funding is often one of the largest long-term family goals. Planning it early makes the overall family strategy stronger and more realistic.
